stage_2_story.text_en:
On Friday afternoon, Moshe's daughter-in-law Rina called him with exciting news. 'Abba, come with us tomorrow! Noam's school is playing in a basketball tournament. He is the team captain this year!' Moshe was delighted. He put on his best jacket and came along with the whole family.

The sports hall was packed with spectators — parents, grandparents, brothers, and sisters all cheering together. Moshe sat in the front row next to Rina and tried to follow the game.

Noam's school was facing a strong opponent from another city. Both teams had clearly worked hard in practice all week. The score changed many times — first it was eight to six, then twelve to twelve, then fifteen to eleven.

At half-time, the coach spoke quietly to the players. He pointed to Noam and said something. Noam nodded, stood up, and addressed his teammates. The captain had spoken.

In the second half, Noam's team played with much more energy. They pulled away and won the match. They were now through to the league final.

After the match, the coach was presented with a small trophy to mark their progress in the tournament. But for Moshe, the real prize was the smile on Noam's face. Walking to the car, Moshe said: 'You are a true champion, Noami. Not because of the score — but because of how you led your friends.'
